name: Zombie apocalypse
desc: Just for fun, but every step is real preparation: day zero, go-bag, home, moving, finding people, a base

guides.w: The news says the dead are walking
s: Don't panic. Panicking people are slow people.
Fill the bath, buckets and bottles with water now: the taps may stop working soon.
Charge everything: phones, power banks, torches, the electric bike.
Get your group together, or tell them where to meet (use your contact plan).
Turn on the radio for official news.
Curtains closed, lights low, doors locked. Then read the next guides.
d: Don't go out to film it for social media
guides.src: Inspired by the US CDC's zombie preparedness campaign

guides.w: When you have to run, grab this
s: Water: at least 3 litres per person, plus a way to clean more (filter or tablets).
Food for 3 days that needs no cooking: nuts, bars, tins with a ring pull.
Torch, wind-up or battery radio, spare batteries, phone and power bank.
First-aid kit and your own medicines for a week.
Copies of ID and important papers, some cash, a paper map.
Warm layer, rain jacket, good shoes, a multitool, a whistle, some rope.
No room for the TV. Or the gaming console. Sorry.
guides.src: Inspired by the US CDC's zombie preparedness campaign

guides.w: Staying in is safer than going out
s: Lock all doors and windows. Block ground-floor windows with furniture or boards.
Make one room upstairs your base, with water, food, a bucket toilet and the radio.
Keep it dark and quiet on the street side: zombies (and burglars) follow light and noise.
Always keep two ways out, and a fire extinguisher or a bucket of water handy.
Take turns sleeping and keeping watch.
d: Never block every exit: fire is a bigger danger than zombies
No candles left alone, no barbecue indoors

guides.w: You have to get from A to B
s: Travel in daylight, and plan your route on the app's offline map before you leave.
A bike beats a car: quiet, fast, doesn't need fuel and gets past blocked roads.
Avoid choke points: bridges, tunnels, narrow streets and big crowds.
Move in pairs, keep talking quietly, and agree what to do if you get separated.
Have a plan B route. And a plan C.
d: Don't take shortcuts through dark places

guides.w: The network is gone. Where is everyone?
s: Go to your agreed meeting point at the agreed time. Wait, then try the second one.
Leave a note or chalk mark: names, the time, and where you went next.
Switch on walkie-talkies at check-in times on your agreed channel.
This app's group keeps working over Bluetooth and text messages when there's no internet.
Texts get through when calls don't.
Water first, always.
Then medicine, first-aid stuff and batteries.
Food in tins and jars, and a tin opener.
Tools: a knife, rope, tape, a lighter, a saw.
Seeds: you'll want to grow food later (see Grow & keep).
Toilet paper is nice, but it won't save you.
d: In a real emergency: take only what you need and share

guides.w: It's been a month. Now what?
s: Water: collect rain, filter it and boil it (see the water guides).
Food: start a vegetable patch, compost your scraps, and learn a few wild plants.
Fire: cook safely outside, and know how to light one without matches.
Keep a routine: jobs, watch shifts, meals at fixed times. It keeps everyone sane.
Teach each other: first aid, knots, map reading. Everything in this app works offline.
1. Cardio. You'll need it.
2. Always carry water.
3. Never split up in the dark.
4. Check the back seat.
5. Read the guides before you need them.
6. Have a plan B and a plan C.
7. Keep your sense of humour.
And if it's a real disaster rather than zombies: follow official advice. It's the same preparation.
